+  "title": "The Green Tree's shoulder light gets its pointed cap",

+  "items": [
+    "The little gabled light over the Green Tree Tavern's enclosed shoulder now comes to a sharp point, the way Andreas's engraving of the inn draws it, instead of the blunt, nearly flat cap it had.",
+    "Its clapboard courses step up the small gable face with it; nothing else about the tavern moves.",
+    "The rest of the left group — the shoulder's own roof slope, and how shoulder, connector and turned range sit against the main block — still differs from the picture, and stays open."
+  ]

+### L-green-tree-shoulder-dormer-cap-2376 — the shoulder light's gable cap
+
+**Covers:** `green_tree_tavern.frame_1833.form.enclosed_left_annex`.
+
+**Decision:** Raise the enclosed shoulder's `front_gable_peak_m` from 4.50 to 4.85 m so the small front-gable light over the shoulder reads as the sharply pointed cap Andreas's detailed retrospective engraving draws, rather than the blunt, nearly flat one the earlier value produced. Against the builder's unchanged 4.20 m dormer head and its 0.625 m roof half-span this turns the cap from about 25.6 to about 46.1 degrees. The picture supplies the triangular SHAPE and nothing else: 4.85 m is a RECONSTRUCTED working control chosen to draw that shape, not a measurement, and the plate carries no scale, dimension, geographic camera or date for it. It establishes no alteration year and no part of the July 1835 condition beyond the earlier reading.
+
+Nothing else moves. The peak stays below the unchanged 5.0 m main-block wall head and far below the model's existing 8.722 m maximum; the dormer's plan extent, its light, the lower sash, the connector, the farther turned range, the main block, the footprint, the world placement, the occupied rings, the door faces, the entrance and the ground contact are all unchanged, and the rebuilt master's full bounding box is exactly equal to the previous one. The remaining shoulder roof slope and the relative proportions of shoulder, connector and range against the main block still differ from the engraving and stay OPEN on T-2376; Trowbridge/Gale's 1902 open wagon bay remains explicit counterevidence to the enclosed shoulder itself, and the conversion date remains unknown. Source ids remain `andreas_1884_green_tree_hotel_plate`, `kurz_allison_1893` and `trowbridge_green_tree_1902`; `chm_green_tree_1859` stays excluded as a geometry witness. The earlier comparison is preserved at `docs/RESEARCH/green-tree-annex-T-2376/andreas_1838-side-by-side-before-dormer-cap-20261104.jpg`. No original-ticket signoff, picture acceptance or new measurement follows.
+
+**Ticket:** T-2376.
+**Recorded:** 2026-11-04.

+## The shoulder light's gable cap — 2026-11-04 (T-2376, partial)
+
+The closed shoulder landed with a front-gable light whose cap was nearly flat: the
+builder sets the dormer wall head from the light itself (3.35 m sill + 0.70 m height
++ 0.15 m head margin = 4.20 m) over a roof half-span of (0.65 m light + 0.50 m cheeks
++ 0.10 m overhang) / 2 = 0.625 m, and a 4.50 m peak over that is a cap of about 25.6
+degrees. Andreas's detailed retrospective engraving draws a small, sharply pointed
+light there. Raising `front_gable_peak_m` to 4.85 m gives about 46.1 degrees and the
+pointed shape; the clapboard courses step up the little gable face with it.
+
+The 4.85 m is a reconstructed control for the drawn shape, not a measurement; the
+plate carries no scale, dimension, camera or date. See
+`docs/LIBERTIES.md` § L-green-tree-shoulder-dormer-cap-2376.
+
+The comparison was controlled: the same camera (`9439f5f7…`) and the same picture
+(`bfaa184f…`), only the master rebuilt. The previous side-by-side is preserved here
+as `andreas_1838-side-by-side-before-dormer-cap-20261104.jpg`; the current one is at
+`docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/green_tree_tavern/andreas_1838-side-by-side.jpg`.
+
+Independent exported-mesh comparison of the two masters confines the change to the
+dormer roof and its gable-course infill: 3,318 → 3,330 triangles; the two dormer
+ridge vertices raised 0.35 m; 24 cladding vertices added in the 4.307–4.581 m band;
+every other primitive byte-identical; and the full model bounding box exactly equal
+(`[-0.25, 0.0, -15.131628] … [18.177464, 8.722019, 0.355]`). No sky seam, hole or
+roof penetration appears in the render. The closed shoulder, its lower sash and
+upper light, and the two separate uncovered farm wagons are retained; no shed, posts
+or covered wagon returns.
+
+**Still open on T-2376.** This fixes one detail only. The shoulder's own roof slope
+and eaves line, and the relative proportions of shoulder, connector and turned range
+against the main block, still differ from Andreas and stay OPEN. Trowbridge/Gale's
+1902 open wagon bay remains explicit counterevidence to the enclosed shoulder, with
+no known conversion date. The upper/attic opening-count disagreement between the
+drawings and the retained camera residuals stay within tolerance (T-3153). The
+original ticket's wider coverage — Andreas 1884, Trowbridge/Gale 1902, CHM c1859
+(unverified, link-only, no geometry) and Kurz & Allison 1893, plus both named
+reproductions — remains incomplete, and no view or ticket is signed off here.
